proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(\gamma=\beta-1/2\), which is positive by the corrected domain \(\beta>1/2\).  Fix the realized sample throughout this proof.  For a candidate \(Q\in\mathcal M\), collect its probability channels, its marked channels divided by \(B_Y\), and its stratum masses in the Hilbert direct sum
\[
 \mathbb H=
 \bigoplus_{x\in\mathcal X}
 \{L^2(\mathcal C_*)\oplus L^2(\mathcal C_*)\oplus\mathbb R\},
 \qquad
 Z_Q=\bigl(F_{x,Q},B_Y^{-1}G_{x,Q},p_{x,Q}\bigr)_{x\in\mathcal X}.
\]
If \(\widehat Z_n\) denotes the analogous empirical vector, the definition of the continuous profile gives the exact identity
\[
 \mathscr D_n(Q)=\|Z_Q-\widehat Z_n\|_{\mathbb H}^2. \tag{1}
\]

We first verify that the subdivisions prescribed by the corrected certificate definition are finite.  Let \(h\) be supported on \(\mathcal A=[-B_A,B_A]\) and satisfy \(\|h\|_{H^\beta}\le R\).  With \(h_T\) denoting the inverse Fourier integral restricted to \(|t|\le T\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|h-h_T\|_\infty
 \le \frac{R}{2\pi}
 \left\{\int_{|t|>T}(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le C R T^{1/2-\beta}=C R T^{-\gamma}. \tag{2}
\]
The integral in (2) is finite precisely because \(\beta>1/2\).  To count a net without discretizing an inverse problem, embed \([-B_A,B_A]\) in the larger interval \([-2B_A,2B_A]\) and periodically extend \(h\) there.  Because \(h\) vanishes off \([-B_A,B_A]\), this extension has Fourier coefficients \((c_\ell)_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}(1+\ell^2)^\beta|c_\ell|^2\le C R^2. \tag{3a}
\]
For its partial Fourier sum \(S_Jh\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|h-S_Jh\|_\infty
 \le \sum_{|\ell|>J}|c_\ell|
 \le C R\left\{\sum_{\ell>J}\ell^{-2\beta}\right\}^{1/2}
 \le C R J^{-\gamma}. \tag{3b}
\]
Choose \(J\asymp u^{-1/\gamma}\) and round each of the \(2J+1\) complex coefficients outward on a grid of mesh \(u/(8J+4)\).  The rounding error in sup norm is at most \(u/2\), while (3b) bounds the truncation error by \(u/2\).  Since every coefficient has modulus at most \(CR\), this supplies a uniform \(u\)-net with at most
\[
 \exp\{C u^{-1/\gamma}\log(C/u)\} \tag{3}
\]
elements.  Applying this construction to each \(f_{x,Q}\) and \(q_{x,Q}\) is legitimate by the density and marked-density Sobolev assumptions.  Because \(f_{x,Q}(a)\ge\kappa>0\) on \(I\), interval division is continuous there and preserves outward inclusion.  The finite-stratum map
\[
 (p,f,q)\longmapsto \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x/f_x \tag{4}
\]
therefore has a finite outward cover of radius \(u\), after changing only a constant depending on \(\kappa\), \(|\mathcal X|\), \(R_f\), \(R_q\), and \(B_Y\).  Explicitly, Sobolev embedding as proved by the same Cauchy--Schwarz calculation at \(T=0\) gives \(\|q_x\|_\infty\le C R_q\), and for denominators \(f,f'\ge\kappa\),
\[
 \left|\frac{q}{f}-\frac{q'}{f'}\right|
 \le \kappa^{-1}|q-q'|+\kappa^{-2}|q'|\,|f-f'|. \tag{4a}
\]
Together with \(0\le p_x\le1\) and the finiteness of \(\mathcal X\), (4a) proves the asserted continuity and the claimed outward-cover radius.

For the error coordinates, the second-moment assumption yields, for every \(T>0\),
\[
 Q(|U_j|>T)\le M_eT^{-2},
 \qquad
 |E_Qe^{isU_j}-E_Qe^{itU_j}|
 \le |s-t|E_Q|U_j|\le \sqrt{M_e}|s-t|. \tag{5}
\]
Thus truncation produces an outward tail disk and the remaining transform is uniformly continuous on the compact protected frequency interval.  The corrected certificate keeps the exact discrepancy and the analytic and tail remainders as outward interval coordinates; it does not replace a tail remainder by zero.  For the normalized truncated law, its vector of monomials through order \(2K_n\) belongs to the convex hull of the compact moment curve: otherwise a separating linear functional would be strictly larger at the barycenter than at every point being averaged, a contradiction.  Hence it has a finite convex representation.  Whenever that representation uses more than \(2K_n+2\) positive weights, affine dependence of the corresponding moment vectors permits a signed perturbation of the weights that preserves every recorded moment and makes at least one weight zero.  Iteration gives a positive atomic quadrature exact through order \(2K_n\); multiplying its weights by the truncated mass restores the original subprobability moments.  Taylor remainder intervals, the tail disk in (5), and outward complex interval arithmetic then cover the exact channel coordinates.  The order-\(K_n\) paired-channel description has at most \(C K_n^2\) coefficient, quadrature, tail, constraint, and analytic-remainder coordinates.  The endpoint cover from (3), used with \(u=\zeta_n\), requires at most \(C\zeta_n^{-1/\gamma}\) further coordinates.  All coordinate ranges are compact after the moment truncation; their radii grow at most polynomially in \(K_n\), \(\tau_n^{-1}\), and \(\zeta_n^{-1}\).  Consequently, dyadic outward subdivision to constraint radius \(\tau_n\) and endpoint radius \(\zeta_n\) stops after finitely many cuts and gives
\[
 |\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|
 \le
 \exp\left\{C\left(K_n^2+\zeta_n^{-1/\gamma}\right)
 \log\left(e+\frac{K_n}{\tau_n\wedge\zeta_n}\right)\right\}. \tag{6}
\]
This also proves termination for every realized sample, because empirical channel values are bounded and continuous on \(\mathcal C_*\), while all comparisons and interval operations use deterministic outward rounding.

We next establish the two set inclusions that repair maximality.  Write \([d_b^-,d_b^+]\) for the outward interval enclosing \(\mathscr D_n(Q)\) for decoded laws in a terminal box \(b\).  Its radius is at most \(\tau_n\), hence its length is at most \(2\tau_n\).  A box is retained only if \(d_b^-\le\epsilon_n^2\), and empty decoded boxes are excluded.  Every \(Q\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) is contained in an outward box, and the box containing it satisfies
\[
 d_b^-\le \mathscr D_n(Q)\le\epsilon_n^2;
\]
it is therefore retained.  This proves \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\subseteq\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}\).  Conversely, if \(Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\) for a retained box, then
\[
 \mathscr D_n(Q)\le d_b^+\le d_b^-+2\tau_n
 \le\epsilon_n^2+2\tau_n. \tag{7}
\]
The corrected definition sets \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\), so (7) also gives \(\mathscr D_n(Q)\le3\epsilon_n^2\).  Since every decoder admits only members of \(\mathcal M\), (7) proves the complete discrepancy sandwich in the statement.

For endpoint validity, fix a retained \(b\) and \(a\in I\).  Every decoded law is in \(\mathcal M\), so its density denominator is at least \(\kappa\) on \(I\).  Hence intersecting the denominator enclosure with \([\kappa,\infty)\) retains every exact denominator and makes interval division valid.  Inclusion isotonicity of outward interval addition, multiplication, and division applied to (4) proves
\[
 \{\mu_Q(a):Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\}\subseteq J_{b,n}(a). \tag{8}
\]
The endpoint stopping rule gives \(\operatorname{rad}J_{b,n}(a)\le\zeta_n\).  Notice that no comparison with an endpoint of the exact profile has been used.

It remains to control the diameter of the certified endpoint profile.  Because the retained collection is finite and each decoded set is nonempty, for any two retained boxes \(b,c\) we may choose witnesses \(Q_b\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\) and \(Q_c\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(c)\).  From (1), (7), and the triangle inequality in \(\mathbb H\),
\[
 \|Z_{Q_b}-Z_{Q_c}\|_{\mathbb H}
 \le \|Z_{Q_b}-\widehat Z_n\|_{\mathbb H}
      +\|Z_{Q_c}-\widehat Z_n\|_{\mathbb H}
 \le 2\sqrt{3}\,\epsilon_n. \tag{9}
\]
For sufficiently large \(n\), the right side is in the small-discrepancy regime of the already-established paired protected inverse theorem.  That theorem and (9) imply
\[
 \sup_{b,c}\|\mu_{Q_b}-\mu_{Q_c}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \le C\left\{
 \frac{\log\log(1/\epsilon_n)}{\log(1/\epsilon_n)}
 \right\}^{\gamma}. \tag{10}
\]
Multiplying the argument of the logarithms by the fixed constant \(2\sqrt3\) changes the right side only by a fixed factor for small \(\epsilon_n\).

Let \(b_-\) attain the finite minimum defining \(\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\), and let \(b_+\) attain the finite maximum defining \(\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\).  By (8) and the radius bound,
\[
 \inf J_{b_-,n}(a)\ge \mu_{Q_{b_-}}(a)-2\zeta_n,
 \qquad
 \sup J_{b_+,n}(a)\le \mu_{Q_{b_+}}(a)+2\zeta_n. \tag{11}
\]
Subtracting in (11) and applying (10) yields, uniformly in \(a\in I\),
\[
 0\le \overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)-\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)
 \le C\left\{
 \frac{\log\log(1/\epsilon_n)}{\log(1/\epsilon_n)}
 \right\}^{\gamma}+4\zeta_n. \tag{12}
\]
Since \(\epsilon_n=C_\alpha\sqrt{\log(en/\alpha)/n}\),
\[
 \log(1/\epsilon_n)=\tfrac12\log n+O(\log\log n),
 \qquad
 \log\log(1/\epsilon_n)=\log\log n+O(1). \tag{13}
\]
The definitions of \(K_n\), \(r_n\), and \(\zeta_n\), with fixed \(c_K>0\), therefore give
\[
 \left\{\frac{\log\log(1/\epsilon_n)}{\log(1/\epsilon_n)}\right\}^{\gamma}
 \le C K_n^{-\gamma}=Cr_n,
 \qquad
 \zeta_n=r_n/\log(en)=o(r_n). \tag{14}
\]
Equations (12)--(14) prove the asserted endpoint-width bound.

Finally, \(\log(en)\asymp K_n\log K_n\), and therefore
\[
 \zeta_n^{-1/\gamma}
 =K_n\{\log(en)\}^{1/\gamma}
 \le C K_n^{1+1/\gamma}(\log K_n)^{1/\gamma}. \tag{15}
\]
When \(\beta>3/2\), one has \(\gamma>1\), so the last expression is at most \(C K_n^2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Substitution into (6) proves the simpler \(K_n^2\) certificate-count regime and completes the proof.

For \(P\in\mathcal M\), define the event
\[
 E_P=\{\mathscr D_n(P)\le\epsilon_n^2\}.
\]
The already-established continuous-channel concentration proposition gives, uniformly over the same model class,
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(E_P)\ge1-\alpha \tag{16}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  On \(E_P\), the true law lies in \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), and the discrepancy sandwich of the corrected finite-profile theorem puts it in \(\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}\).  Thus it lies in a retained box with a nonempty decoded law set.  The interval inclusion in that theorem gives, simultaneously for all \(a\in I\),
\[
 \underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)
 \le \mu_P(a)
 \le \overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a). \tag{17}
\]
Consistency and the bounded-potential-outcome assumption imply \(|\mu_P(a)|\le B_Y\).  Hence the additional outward displacement by \(\zeta_n\) and clipping to \([-B_Y,B_Y]\) in the definition of \((L_n,U_n)\) cannot remove \(\mu_P(a)\) from the interval.  Equations (16)--(17) prove
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu_P(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}
 \ge1-\alpha. \tag{18}
\]
The corrected algorithm consists of finitely many outward rational interval operations with deterministic tie-breaking, so its endpoints are jointly measurable.  Each \(J_{b,n}(a)\) is a subinterval of \([-B_Y,B_Y]\), and the global minimum of its lower endpoints cannot exceed the global maximum of its upper endpoints.  It follows directly from the clipping formulas that \(L_n\le U_n\).  Thus (18) verifies every condition in the definition of \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\).

The width is controlled on every sample.  If the certified profile is empty, its definition gives \(L_n=U_n=0\).  Otherwise, clipping can only reduce width, and the certified endpoint-diameter conclusion gives
\[
 W_n
 \le \sup_{a\in I}
 \{\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)-\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)+2\zeta_n\}
 \le C r_n. \tag{19}
\]
This step uses the inverse modulus on the enlarged discrepancy profile; it does not assert that a certified endpoint is within \(O(\zeta_n)\) of the corresponding exact-profile endpoint.  Taking expectations in the deterministic inequality (19), followed by the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M\), yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le Cr_n.
\]
Together with (18), this proves the theorem.

The corrected certified band is a single data-dependent member of \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\).  The upper-band theorem and the definition of minimax expected maximal width therefore give
\[
 \mathfrak R_n
 \le \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]
 \le Cr_n. \tag{20}
\]

For the converse, fix any \((L_n,U_n)\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\) and take \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\in\mathcal M\) from the already-established fixed-nuisance marked-pair theorem.  For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), let
\[
 A_j=\{L_n(a)\le\mu_{j,n}(a)\le U_n(a)
          \text{ for every }a\in I\}.
\]
Uniform honesty gives
\[
 P_{j,n,\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(A_j)\ge1-\alpha. \tag{21}
\]
The total-variation inequality \(R(A)\ge S(A)-\|R-S\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), applied to the event \(A_1\), and the marked-pair bound imply
\[
 P_{0,n,\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(A_1)
 \ge P_{1,n,\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(A_1)-\eta
 \ge1-\alpha-\eta. \tag{22}
\]
Combining (21) for \(j=0\) with (22) and the union bound yields
\[
 P_{0,n,\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(A_0\cap A_1)
 \ge1-2\alpha-\eta>0, \tag{23}
\]
where strict positivity is exactly the declared restriction \(\eta<1-2\alpha\).  On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the band contains both curves at every \(a\), and hence
\[
 W_n\ge\sup_{a\in I}|\mu_{1,n}(a)-\mu_{0,n}(a)|\ge cr_n. \tag{24}
\]
Taking the expectation of (24) under \(P_{0,n,\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\) and using (23) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]
 \ge c(1-2\alpha-\eta)r_n. \tag{25}
\]
The band in (25) was arbitrary, so taking the infimum over \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\) proves the lower bound.

For the equivalent rate display, the corrected smoothness domain gives \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>0\).  Since \(c_K\) is fixed and positive, the definition of \(K_n\) implies
\[
 K_n\asymp\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 r_n=K_n^{1/2-\beta}=K_n^{-\gamma}
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right\}^{\beta-1/2}.
\]
Combining this identity with (20) and (25) completes the proof for every fixed \(\beta>1/2\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
There is a constant \(C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed constants of \(\mathcal M\), such that the corrected two-tolerance certified algorithm terminates for every sample and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), returns a finite collection \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\) satisfying
\[
 \Theta_{n,\alpha}\subseteq\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}=\bigcup_{b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}}\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\subseteq\{Q\in\mathcal M:\mathscr D_n(Q)\le\epsilon_n^2+2\tau_n\}\subseteq\{Q\in\mathcal M:\mathscr D_n(Q)\le C\epsilon_n^2\}.
\]
Every retained box has \(\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\ne\varnothing\), and, for every \(a\in I\),
\[
 \{\mu_Q(a):Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\}\subseteq J_{b,n}(a),\qquad \operatorname{rad}J_{b,n}(a)\le\zeta_n.
\]
Consequently, whenever \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 0\le\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)-\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\le C\left[\left\{\frac{\log\log(1/\epsilon_n)}{\log(1/\epsilon_n)}\right\}^{\beta-1/2}+\zeta_n\right]\le Cr_n
\]
uniformly over \(a\in I\). Writing \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>0\), the certificate count obeys
\[
 |\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|\le\exp\left\{C\left(K_n^2+\zeta_n^{-1/\gamma}\right)\log\left(e+\frac{K_n}{\tau_n\wedge\zeta_n}\right)\right\}.
\]
In the simpler regime \(\beta>3/2\), this becomes
\[
 |\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|\le\exp\left\{CK_n^2\log\left(e+\frac{K_n}{\tau_n\wedge\zeta_n}\right)\right\}.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former exact-profile endpoint-proximity assertion does not follow from outward feasibility: a retained box may represent only laws just outside the exact threshold. The corrected claim keeps exact-profile coverage, proves that every decoded law lies in an enlarged profile with discrepancy at most \(\epsilon_n^2+2\tau_n\), excludes empty decoded boxes, and controls certified endpoint width by applying the proved inverse modulus to feasible decoded witnesses. The certificate count must also expose both tolerances and the Sobolev entropy term when \(1/2<\beta\le3/2\).

proposed.statement:
There is a constant \(C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed constants of \(\mathcal M\), such that the corrected two-tolerance certified algorithm terminates for every sample and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), returns a finite collection \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\) satisfying
\[
 \Theta_{n,\alpha}
 \subseteq \Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}
 =\bigcup_{b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}}\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)
 \subseteq
 \{Q\in\mathcal M:\mathscr D_n(Q)\le \epsilon_n^2+2\tau_n\}
 \subseteq
 \{Q\in\mathcal M:\mathscr D_n(Q)\le C\epsilon_n^2\}.
\]
Every retained box has \(\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\ne\varnothing\), and, for every \(a\in I\),
\[
 \{\mu_Q(a):Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\}\subseteq J_{b,n}(a),
 \qquad \operatorname{rad}J_{b,n}(a)\le\zeta_n.
\]
Consequently, whenever \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 0\le
 \overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)-\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)
 \le C\left[
 \left\{\frac{\log\log(1/\epsilon_n)}{\log(1/\epsilon_n)}\right\}^{\beta-1/2}
 +\zeta_n\right]
 \le C r_n
\]
uniformly over \(a\in I\).  Writing \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>0\), the certificate count obeys
\[
 |\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|
 \le
 \exp\left\{C\left(K_n^2+\zeta_n^{-1/\gamma}\right)
 \log\left(e+\frac{K_n}{\tau_n\wedge\zeta_n}\right)\right\}.
\]
In the simpler regime \(\beta>3/2\), this becomes
\[
 |\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|
 \le
 \exp\left\{C K_n^2
 \log\left(e+\frac{K_n}{\tau_n\wedge\zeta_n}\right)\right\}.
\]
proposed.justification: Honesty is operational only if every exact-profile law is enclosed, every endpoint box has a decoded feasible witness, and all represented laws remain within a controlled enlargement of the empirical discrepancy profile.
proposed.gap: Kato, Sasaki, and Ura implement a finite-frequency inversion but do not certify a continuum law-valued profile; Neumann uses a continuous metric without a finite outer optimization or a two-tolerance maximality guarantee.
proposed.consumer: Empirical users obtain reproducible outward endpoints whose total width is certified at the statistical inverse-modulus scale, while numerical endpoint tolerance remains asymptotically negligible.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed theorem uses the new constraint tolerance, adds the inverse theorem as a declared dependency, records all newly used symbols, removes unsupported exact-endpoint proximity, and states the corrected two-tolerance certificate count.

prose_updates.tldr: The observed law contains an unmarked probability channel and an outcome-marked signed channel. Continuous integrated control of both channels on a moment-derived protected frequency square, followed by quantitative analytic continuation and Sobolev recovery, yields an honest simultaneous ADRF band with minimax expected maximal width \(r_n\asymp(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\) for every fixed \(\beta>1/2\). A terminating outward-rounded profile uses a constraint tolerance \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\) and a separate endpoint tolerance \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\): it outer-covers the exact profile, retains only nonempty decoded boxes, and confines every decoded law to a constant-factor enlarged discrepancy profile. The band width is obtained directly from the protected inverse modulus, without claiming numerical proximity to exact-profile extrema. A fixed-density Bernoulli marked experiment built from a weighted Jacobi packet and fixed asymmetric \(\operatorname{sinc}^4\)-mixture errors supplies the matching lower bound.

project_justification.gap: Colangelo and Lee give uniform-in-treatment ADRF inference when treatment is measured without error, and known-error measurement-error methods give pointwise ADRF inference. Blind repeated-measurement methods identify and estimate an unmarked density, and robust Kotlarski methods invert finite complex moments for density bands. None gives an honest whole-curve ADRF band, a sharp expected-width modulus, or a fixed-nuisance marked converse when two replicate errors are unknown, asymmetric, nonidentical, and allowed to have spectral zeros; nor do they provide a finite law-valued outer certificate with distinct statistical-feasibility and endpoint tolerances.
project_justification.niche: Compact dose support makes both the density transform and the signed marked transform entire. A common second-moment radius supplies a uniform nonvanishing neighborhood by \(|\varphi_j(t)|\ge1-|t|\sqrt{M_e}\), so the protected square follows from a law-level moment condition. The inferential object is a paired nonlinear quotient, and certificate maximality is secured by a discrepancy sandwich rather than by proximity to an exact optimizer.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the paired protected inverse at the sharp sup-norm exponent, embeds it in a continuously constrained confidence profile, and certifies a finite decoded outer profile using \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\) for constraints and \(\zeta_n\) for endpoint arithmetic. Every retained endpoint box has a decoded feasible law, all decoded laws lie in a constant-factor enlarged discrepancy profile, and the inverse modulus therefore bounds the full certified endpoint diameter. A weighted Jacobi Bernoulli marked packet with fixed asymmetric \(\operatorname{sinc}^4\)-mixture errors matches the upper width while leaving the complete unmarked replicate law fixed.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The probability and signed marked channels are controlled by continuous integrated empirical contrasts on \(\mathcal C_*\). Entire-transform continuation and Sobolev recovery are profiled jointly. An outward finite certificate uses \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\) for discrepancy constraints and \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\) for ADRF endpoint evaluation, discards boxes with empty decoded law sets, and bounds width through the enlarged-profile inverse modulus.

prose_updates.related_work: Colangelo and Lee (2025), especially Supplementary Theorems S11 and S12 on pages 63--65 of the public manuscript, are the closest published uniform-in-treatment ADRF comparator: they derive a uniform asymptotically linear representation and multiplier-bootstrap inference over a compact treatment set when treatment is measured without error. Thus whole-curve ADRF inference itself is not the new obstacle; the obstacle is simultaneous inference after blind deconvolution with two unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric replicate errors. Huang and Zhang (2023) motivate the continuous-treatment measurement-error problem and derive pointwise ADRF inference when the error transform is known; their operator is not blind and their result is not simultaneous. Gao, Bondell, Huang, and Gong (2024) estimate a latent-treatment ADRF through a variational neural model, without a blind-replicate identification or honest-band theorem. Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy (2025) provide the closest method exemplar: their continuous integrated analytic-polynomial contrast achieves a nearly parametric local transform error and analytic continuation yields an unmarked density rate. The present construction adds a signed marked channel, a quotient, supremum loss, honest coverage, and a fixed-nuisance converse; its lower packet is a weighted Jacobi reproducing-kernel construction paired with new fixed asymmetric \(\operatorname{sinc}^4\)-mixture errors, rather than a transplant of the comparator's density-packet construction. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura (2021) show how test inversion avoids fragile closed-form Kotlarski division, but their finite moments target an unmarked density and do not certify a continuum profile or sharp width. Kato and Sasaki (2018, 2019) supply Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap machinery for density and errors-in-variables regression bands under auxiliary, symmetric, or conventional spectral information. Neumann (2007) motivates integrated characteristic functions as continuous probability coordinates. Lounici and Nickl (2011), Genovese and Wasserman (2008), and Low (1997) inform the sup-norm packing and band-width reduction. The Colangelo--Lee comparison is informed-by rather than a claimed tightening; the only equivalence claim is the explicit error-free reduction in Theorem 9.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite certificate must keep two numerical scales separate. Constraint boxes are refined to \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\), while ADRF evaluations are refined to \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\); outward feasibility alone does not place a numerical endpoint within \(O(\zeta_n)\) of an exact-profile extremum. Width instead follows by putting all nonempty decoded boxes inside a constant-factor enlarged discrepancy profile and applying the proved protected inverse modulus to decoded witnesses. For \(1/2<\beta\le3/2\), endpoint covering entropy enlarges the worst-case finite-certificate count; only \(\beta>3/2\) yields the simpler \(K_n^2\) coordinate regime. On the converse side, the weighted Jacobi packet must preserve the Bernoulli range, strict Sobolev slack, fixed nuisance laws, and product-law total variation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The frontier holds for every fixed \(\beta>1/2\), with the support interval, Sobolev radii, overlap constants, outcome bound, and common error second-moment radius fixed. Error distributions remain unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric, and may have zero sets away from the moment-derived protected neighborhood. The finite certificate terminates throughout this range, although its simpler \(K_n^2\) complexity regime requires \(\beta>3/2\). Adaptation to unknown smoothness or drifting channel severity is outside the theorem. When \(U_1=U_2=0\), Theorem 9 recovers the standard error-free g-formula.

statement_notes.justification: Honesty is operational only if every exact-profile law is enclosed, every endpoint box has a decoded feasible witness, and every represented law remains in a controlled enlarged profile.
statement_notes.gap: Existing finite-frequency inversions do not establish a continuum law-valued discrepancy sandwich with separate constraint and endpoint tolerances.
statement_notes.consumer: Users receive finite outward endpoints whose full diameter, rather than an unsupported distance to exact extrema, is certified at the statistical inverse-modulus scale.

statement_notes.justification: This is the constructive half of the simultaneous-band frontier; its coverage uses exact-profile outer inclusion and its width uses the enlarged-profile inverse modulus.
statement_notes.gap: Existing ADRF or deconvolution bands do not handle blind asymmetric replicate errors with spectral zeros while also certifying continuum profile feasibility.
statement_notes.consumer: Studies with two nonidentical replicate measurements can report a uniformly valid ADRF band with a worst-case width guarantee for every fixed \(\beta>1/2\).

statement_notes.justification: The matching expected-maximal-width theorem combines the certified upper band with a fixed-density, fixed-error marked testing pair.
statement_notes.gap: No cited work matches an honest ADRF sup-band upper bound to a fixed-nuisance marked lower bound under fully blind asymmetric replicates with spectral zeros.
statement_notes.consumer: Study designers can translate the frontier into sample-size requirements across the full regularity range \(\beta>1/2\).
